title: Mild Chicken Pad Thai
subtitle: chewy rice noodles with chicken, egg and bean sprouts in a sweet-tangy sauce, topped with crunchy peanuts and lime, no chilies
imageAlt: Glossy rice noodles with chicken, egg, bean sprouts and chopped peanuts with a lime wedge in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Have everything cut and the sauce mixed before you start; it cooks in 10 minutes.
Fish sauce smells strong in the bottle but tastes savoury, not fishy, once cooked.

steps.title: Soak the noodles
steps.text: Cover the noodles with very hot tap water and soak 8–10 minutes, until bendy but still firm. Drain.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Juice 1 lime and cut the other in wedges. Whisk the fish sauce, brown sugar, 2 tbsp lime juice, soy sauce and water until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Chicken
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Stir-fry the chicken 4–5 minutes, until no longer pink and 74°C (165°F). Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then move everything to one side.

steps.title: Egg
steps.text: Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the empty side, pour in the eggs and scramble until just set, then stir through the chicken.

steps.title: Noodles
steps.text: Add the noodles and sauce and toss 2–3 minutes with tongs, until the noodles are tender and have soaked up the sauce. Toss in the bean sprouts for the last 30 seconds.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with the chopped peanuts and serve with lime wedges.

fixIt.fix: They soaked too long or in boiling water. Hot tap water, and drain while still firm; they finish in the pan.
Toss them with a teaspoon of oil after draining, and use tongs in the pan.
Adjust with lime juice; taste the sauce before it goes in.

saleTip: Rice noodles and fish sauce are in No Frills' international aisle and keep for months; one bottle of fish sauce lasts ages.
swap: Shrimp instead of chicken: 450 g, stir-fried 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque, 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Add a splash of water before microwaving; rice noodles firm up in the fridge.
doneness: Chicken at 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, poultry pieces); eggs scrambled until set.
source: Based on tested home pad Thai methods (Hot Thai Kitchen's beginner version, Budget Bytes): soaked rice noodles, a fish sauce, sugar and lime sauce (in place of tamarind), chicken, egg and bean sprouts. No dried chilies.
prepAhead: Slice the chicken and mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead.
reheat: Covered in the microwave with 1 tbsp water, 2 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Chicken, egg and noodles in the sauce; no sprouts or peanuts.

stepNotes.5: Basic: serve with lime wedges only.

fancy.note: Shrimp and chicken together, the restaurant way.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: add the shrimp with the garlic and stir-fry 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque, 74°C (165°F).

plating: Noodles twirled high in shallow bowls.
Peanuts in a line across the top.

why.1-0: Fish sauce is the salty, savoury backbone of pad Thai.
why.1-2: Lime stands in for tamarind for the tangy note, and it's easy to find.
why.0-0: Soaking instead of boiling keeps rice noodles chewy, not mushy.

funFact: Pad Thai was promoted as a national dish by the Thai government in the 1930s and 40s.

keeps.note: rice noodles go brittle when frozen
